newsitem.title: ITALY: Eight held in alleged Mafia plot to kill judge.
newsitem.headline: Eight held in alleged Mafia plot to kill judge.

text.p: Police said on Tuesday they had discovered a plot to kill one of Italy's leading anti-Mafia prosecutors and had arrested eight suspected Mafiosi.

Police said wiretapped telephone conversations in a butcher's shop revealed that the Mafia had approached a driver who worked for the public prosecutor's office in the Sicilian capital Palermo because it wanted a contact inside the court.
The Mob asked the driver, who worked for the magistrate who presided over a key Mafia maxi-trial in the 1980s, to plant a bomb in the armoured car of chief prosecutor Giancarlo Caselli.
The butcher was subsequently arrested and his two interlocutors were suspected Mafia members, police said. The murder plot, which dated back to 1995, was not carried out.
Police said the eight detainees were being held on charges of Mafia association and aiding and abetting Mafiosi on the run.

Politicians said the news proved that despite last year's arrest of Giovanni Brusca, one of the most senior Mafiosi captured in years and considered a major victory for the state, Italians would be wrong to dismiss the Mafia as dead.
"I've always said that the capture of Brusca didn't mean we could talk of an end to the fight against Cosa Nostra," Interior Minister Giovanni Napolitano said.
"It would be a grave error to lower our guard," echoed Pietro Folena, a senior member of the Democratic Party of the Left, the biggest in Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government.
"All this is yet more proof that the power of Cosa Nostra is largely intact, even though it has been decapitated," said Pino Arlacchi, a leftist senator and Mafia expert.
Italy arrested the Mafia's "boss of bosses", Salvatore Riina, four years ago after 23 years on the run.
Two prominent anti-Mafia prosecutors, Giovanni Falcone and Paolo Borsellino, were killed within months of each other in Palermo in 1992 in separate bomb attacks that horrified Italy.
